newsitem.title: GERMANY: UPS says Euro will cut freight prices.
newsitem.headline: UPS says Euro will cut freight prices.

text.p: Freight transport prices in Europe will fall with the introduction of the single European currency, the Euro, from 1999, a senior United Parcel Service manager forecast.
Dieter Murowski, UPS European marketing director, said European transport prices would in future only be measured by weight and distance as national price-lists were replaced by European tariffs.

UPS expected the single currency to promote growth in the medium-term and thus increase demand for transport and logistics services in a single European distribution market, he told a conference on European currency union and the freight industry.

"We expect overall that prices will fall. Transparency through the Euro will bring prices down and international, cross-border bids will be made. Foreign consignments will not be fundamentally more expensive than domestic consignments," Murowski forecast.
He added: "A common European market demands a European price-list. The introduction of the Euro will make a new tariff structure not only necessary but unavoidable."

UPS itself aimed to have all preparations for the currency switch finished by October 1, 1998, as some large clients would switch to the Euro at once while smaller companies would wait and then be forced to follow, he said.

"We will offer in both Euros and in national currencies so the client has the choice how he wants to pay. Our clients must be able to assume they can pay UPS in Euros from January 1, 1999, if they want to," he said.

UPS had set up a cross-department Euro team to analyse consequences of the Euro for clients, the market and UPS, to develop a change-over strategy and timetable and to monitor its implementation. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
